audit_scope.description: This batch covers CL beacon chain blob scheduling and proposer lookahead (Fulu), EL precompile execution (MODEXP with Prague and EIP-7823 bounds), EL EVM interpreter (Prague), EL fork activation (fork_criteria, EIP-1013 Constantinople), wallet/DApp interaction APIs (EIP-5792 batched calls, EIP-2831 tx replacement events), EIP governance versioning (EIP-7577), and P2P messaging (EIP-627 Whisper).

out_of_scope: Full opcode handler implementations beyond interpreter dispatch

in_scope: Fulu Fork Digest with Blob Parameters
out_of_scope: Full beacon state transition beyond Fulu blob/proposer mechanisms

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed batched calls, exploit capability fingerprinting, resource exhaustion via wallet API, forge replacement transaction events
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks, exploit fork activation boundary edge cases, Whisper envelope flooding, malformed envelope injection
Submit oversized MODEXP inputs to trigger consensus bugs, craft inputs exploiting gas underpricing, stack depth exhaustion attacks via recursive calls

cl_vectors.threat: Propose blocks with invalid blob counts exceeding epoch-specific limits, manipulate proposer lookahead, exploit fork digest mismatch to partition network

cl_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoint)
cl_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect data, censorship, denial of service

misclassified_entities.reason: The Ethereum blockchain is not external to the system under audit; it is the system itself. EIP-5792 models wallet interaction, where the blockchain is the execution environment, not an external entity sending data into the system.
EIP authors operate in the governance/specification domain, not as runtime external entities sending data into a live system. EIP-7577 versioning is a process specification, not a runtime protocol.
Pull request submitters interact with GitHub repository tooling, not with the Ethereum protocol runtime. This is a governance process entity.
Repository CI/CD tooling is part of the EIP governance process, not a runtime entity interacting with Ethereum protocol components.

Incoming block data is not an external entity per se; it is data produced by block producers (miners/validators) and propagated by peers. The actual external entities are the block producers and peer nodes.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps connect to wallets via JSON-RPC provider interface. No authentication beyond basic connection authorization. DApps can submit arbitrary call batches, query capabilities for fingerprinting, and provide malformed parameters. All input must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via UI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet UI (approve/reject dialogs for EIP-5792 batches, tx speedup/cancel via EIP-2831)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The user is authenticated by wallet ownership but may not fully understand transaction implications. User decisions (approve/reject, speedup, cancel) are trusted as intentional but the wallet must ensure accurate information display.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp Event Listener via Provider Events
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Provider event subscription (tx_speedup, tx_cancel, tx_replacement events per EIP-2831)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps listening for transaction replacement events are untrusted consumers. The provider must not leak cross-application information through events. Event data must be scoped to the requesting application.

trusted_external_entities.name: Fingerprinting Attacker via Capability Query
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious actors can use capability queries to fingerprint wallet types and identify targets. Wallet must filter sensitive capabilities for untrusted callers to prevent identification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Caller via MODEXP Precompile
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can call the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input data. Inputs include length fields, base, exponent, and modulus which are all attacker-controlled. EIP-7823 bounds (1024 bytes) must be enforced. Gas pricing must accurately reflect computation cost. Zero-padding for short inputs must be handled correctly.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker via Oversized MODEXP Input
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CALL to address 0x05 with length fields > 1024 bytes
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker deliberately submits inputs exceeding EIP-7823 bounds to exploit potential consensus bugs or resource exhaustion. The precompile must reject and consume all gas.

trusted_external_entities.name: Message Caller via EVM Interpreter
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM message call (CREATE, CALL, DELEGATECALL, etc.)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any entity can initiate EVM message calls with arbitrary code and data. Stack depth limits (1024), gas accounting, code size limits (24576 bytes), and 0xEF prefix rejection must be enforced. Recursive calls and gas exhaustion are primary attack vectors.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks that must be validated against fork-specific rules. Peers are unauthenticated and can send blocks crafted to exploit fork activation boundary conditions (e.g., incorrect fork rule selection at Constantinople block 7,280,000).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner/Validator) via Block Production
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block production and propagation at fork boundaries
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers trigger fork activation when producing blocks at or above activation thresholds. Malicious producers could attempt to manipulate timestamps (post-merge) to influence fork activation timing.

trusted_external_entities.name: Whisper Network Peer via DEVp2p
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Whisper protocol messages (status 0x00, envelopes 0x01, PoW update 0x02, bloom update 0x03)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Whisper peers are unauthenticated P2P participants. They can send malformed envelopes, invalid PoW values (NaN, INF, negative), flood with low-quality messages, or attempt traffic analysis through bloom filter correlation. All envelopes must be validated for structure, PoW, and topic matching.

trusted_external_entities.name: Whisper Application via Local API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Local applications submitting messages through Whisper are semi-trusted (authenticated local access) but message content and encryption parameters must still be validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via Beacon Block Proposal (Fulu)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Beacon block proposal with blob commitments
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators proposing blocks with blob KZG commitments are untrusted. The CL must validate that blob commitment count does not exceed the epoch-specific limit from BLOB_SCHEDULE (15 at epoch 412672, 21 at epoch 419072). Incorrect blob count enforcement could cause chain splits.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full validation of request schema, version, chainId format, call array structure, bundle size limits, capability support, atomicity requirements, and duplicate ID detection. Application identity must be verified to prevent cross-app status leakage.
Authorization check (error 4100 if unauthorized). Capability filtering for untrusted callers to prevent wallet fingerprinting. Address must match enabled account.
Sensitive capabilities must be filtered for untrusted callers. Response must not uniquely identify wallet type or configuration.

Speed-up invariants must be validated: same nonce, recipient, value, data with minimum 10% gas increase. Cancel must construct valid self-send. User approval UI must accurately represent transaction details.

Events must be scoped per-application to prevent cross-app information leakage. Event data (oldTx, newTx, nonce, from) must be accurate. Replacement type classification (speedup vs cancel vs generic) must be correct.

All three length fields must be validated <= 1024 bytes per EIP-7823. Gas cost must accurately reflect computation complexity. Zero modulus, zero exponent, zero base edge cases must be handled. Short input must be zero-padded. Output must be exactly modulus_length bytes.

Inputs with any length field > 1024 bytes must be immediately rejected. All gas allocated to the call must be consumed on violation. Error status must be returned. Length check must occur before complex gas pricing calculation.

Stack depth must be validated (depth <= 1024). Contract creation must check address collision, validate no 0xEF prefix, enforce MAX_CODE_SIZE (24576 bytes), charge code deposit gas. ExceptionalHalt must consume all gas. Revert must preserve gas but rollback state. EIP-7702 authorizations must be properly validated.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P block validation with fork criteria
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block must be validated against correct fork rules determined by block number (pre-merge) or timestamp (post-merge). Fork criteria ordering must be deterministic. Constantinople activation at correct network-specific block heights. Invalid blocks must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block production at fork activation boundary
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block at or above fork threshold must activate all constituent EIPs atomically. Timestamp-based activation (post-merge) must account for potential timestamp manipulation. All 5 Constantinople EIPs must activate simultaneously at fork block.

Full envelope structure validation: [Expiry(4), TTL(4), Topic(4), Data(var), Nonce(8)]. PoW must meet minimum requirement and not be NaN/INF/negative. Topic must match bloom filter. Protocol violations must trigger peer disconnection. Unknown packet codes must be silently ignored.
Message encryption (ECIES or AES-GCM) and ECDSA signing must be applied correctly. 256-byte padding must be applied to prevent size-based metadata leakage.

Blob KZG commitment count must not exceed get_blob_parameters(epoch).max_blobs_per_block. The BLOB_SCHEDULE lookup must correctly find the largest scheduled epoch <= current epoch. All nodes must agree on BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration to prevent network partitioning.
